question: A library splits its books between branches by the first letter of the title: A–E, F–J, and so on. A hugely popular new series starting with "H" arrives. What happens?
options: The F–J branch gets most of the visitors while the others stay quiet
Visitors spread evenly because every branch has many books
The books of the series are shared between all branches
Nothing changes, because the series is only a few books
explanation: Splitting by ranges of a key keeps similar keys together, so everything that starts with "H" goes to one branch, and so do its visitors. That is a hot partition. Splitting by a scrambled number from the title (a hash) would have spread the series' visitors, at the cost of making "all titles from A to C" a visit to every branch.
